newsitem.title: GERMANY: German soya crusher carries on after gene protest.
newsitem.headline: German soya crusher carries on after gene protest.

text.p: German oilseeds crusher Oelmuehle Hamburg AG (Oelag) would stick to winter processing schedules which included genetically altered U.S. soybeans, board chief Arnd von Wissel said on Wednesday.
This followed protests by Greenpeace environmentalists late on Tuesday when the freighter Ideal Progress arrived at Oelag silos to discharge 44,600 tonnes of U.S. new crop beans.
"The ship docked here as planned and is in the process of offloading, we have not taken notice of the Greenpeace action," von Wissel said in response to an enquiry.
Soymeal and oil made from the U.S. beans would be dispatched to customers from November 11.
Further U.S. cargoes had been ordered from crushers across Europe and would arrive roughly at 10 day intervals over the next few months. The Atlantic trip takes about 20 days.
The protestors said they would continue to put pressure on processors of the soybeans and their customers because possible damage to public health could not be excluded.
But von Wissel said his food industry clients had not requested him to provide products from unmodified soybeans.
"They have realised we cannot replace U.S. soybeans, there have been part replacements with rapeseed products but by and large it is impossible to go without U.S. supplies."

Asked if he had turned to customers in a bid to jointly tackle public scepticism, he said, "I acknowledge it is difficult for them (the food industry) ...they have to think more carefully about their brands' images than a processor of raw materials."
Von Wissel said there had been sporadic offers of soybeans guaranteed free from genetically modified beans in sizes ranging from 5,000 tonnes 20,000 tonnes.
"But I need 170,000 tonnes a month and if 10,000 were from traditional beans you would not be able to find them," he said.
"But it's unnecessary anyway because there is good international demand for soy oil without special requirements."
Oelag, controlled by ADM Archer Daniels Midland Co, lat year accounted for 2.66 million tonnes of soybeans, rape and sunseed processing out of a total German crush of seven million.
